findings.body:
The handler looks up whichever `accountId` the client puts in the JSON body, with no check that the caller is staff or owns that account. An authenticated user who posts `{"accountId":"<victim-id>"}` receives that account's record.

Authorize the override: honor `body.accountId` only when `auth()` shows the caller is staff (or has an equivalent account-read grant); otherwise always look up `caller.accountId` and return 403 for a cross-account request.

summary:
Any authenticated caller can now load another account by putting `accountId` in the JSON body. `getAccount` still authenticates, then uses that client-supplied id with no staff or ownership check, so this is an IDOR on a previously self-scoped lookup.

The comment on `src/routes/account.ts:6` describes a staff-tools use case, but the handler never inspects a role or permission from `auth()`. This workspace has no router or `auth` implementation to confine the endpoint to staff, so the override is reachable by whoever can call `getAccount`.

Honor `body.accountId` only after an explicit staff/authorization check from `auth()`; otherwise keep looking up `caller.accountId`. Reject cross-account requests with 403.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The patch changed getAccount from always using caller.accountId to body.accountId ?? caller.accountId with no staff/ownership check, so any authenticated client can fetch another account’s record by posting a victim id. That is a real IDOR; critical severity is appropriate.
